network.tdh.verify.metadataDescription: Every day, Rust, Python and 6529.io TDH side by side, with every difference explained.
network.tdh.verify.title: TDH verification
network.tdh.verify.lede: Every day, the TDH of every collector is computed three ways and compared: by the validators’ Rust core, by the Python reference, and by 6529.io’s current backend. This page shows the results, including every difference and its explanation. Holders are never named.
network.tdh.verify.sample.title: Sample data, not a measurement.
network.tdh.verify.sample.body: The Rust and 6529.io figures are from the independent comparison of 14 and 15 October 2026. The Python figures are copied from Rust to show the layout and were not computed. Daily reports replace this sample when their data source is connected.
network.tdh.verify.awaiting.title: Daily reports start on 16 October 2026.
network.tdh.verify.awaiting.body: The first one appears here after its run. Until then, the evidence behind TDH-v1 is on the specification page.

network.tdh.verify.diff.heading: Differences
network.tdh.verify.diff.lede: A difference is any record whose values are not equal in every field. Each one gets a class and, when known, a cause. Holders are shown as labels only.
network.tdh.verify.diff.emptyFiltered: No differences in this class on this day.

network.tdh.verify.diff.label: Label
network.tdh.verify.diff.missingNote: — {missing}: the day’s file does not carry these per-holder values.
network.tdh.verify.class.A.body: Explained by a deliberate difference between TDH-v1 and the old backend (a DEV item).
network.tdh.verify.class.B.body: Explained by a known issue in the old backend (a BUG item).
network.tdh.verify.class.C.body: A defect in the new software, for example Rust and Python disagree.
network.tdh.verify.class.D.body: Every difference starts here until it is classified.
network.tdh.verify.class.note: Class A and B differences are explained, not accepted: the owner still decides what to do with each.
network.tdh.verify.cause.DEV-2: A token left a wallet and came back within one transaction. 6529.io’s backend never counted it as gone, so the wallet kept the copy’s age; the Rust core applies every movement in order, so the age restarted. Decision D131 settles this: ownership is read at transaction boundaries, so a copy that leaves and returns inside one transaction never left. Once the Rust core nets within a transaction, these values agree.

network.tdh.verify.method.heading: How this works
network.tdh.verify.method.snapshot.title: The same snapshot.
network.tdh.verify.method.snapshot.body: All three use the snapshot block of the day, the last Ethereum block before 00:00 UTC.
network.tdh.verify.method.inputs.title: Independent inputs.
network.tdh.verify.method.inputs.body: The Rust core and the Python reference read the day’s events from Ethereum and compute TDH-v1. 6529.io’s values come from the files it publishes every day on Arweave. 6529.io’s values are the object under test, never an input.
network.tdh.verify.method.exact.title: Exact comparison.
network.tdh.verify.method.exact.body: Every field of every identity and wallet is compared for exact equality, with no tolerance.
network.tdh.verify.method.classes.title: Classification.
network.tdh.verify.method.classes.body: Each difference is classified A to D.
network.tdh.verify.method.after.title: After the cutover,
network.tdh.verify.method.after.body: 6529.io runs the Rust core, so their agreement shows that what is published is what was computed. The Python reference stays the independent check of the computation.
network.tdh.verify.method.validators: Validators run the same comparison on their own, after they have signed, so 6529.io’s values can never influence their vote.
network.tdh.verify.flow.title: The daily comparison
network.tdh.verify.flow.desc: Ethereum feeds the Rust core and the Python reference. 6529.io’s backend publishes its upload on Arweave. All three meet in the comparison, which publishes the files this page reads.
network.tdh.verify.flow.sameCode: After the cutover, the 6529.io backend runs the same Rust core.
network.tdh.verify.flow.text: Ethereum → Rust core and Python reference → Compare. 6529.io backend → Arweave upload → Compare. Compare → published JSON → this page. After the cutover, the 6529.io backend runs the Rust core.
